headline: PM vows to build Bangladesh into trillion-dollar, climate-resilient economy

body_html:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday vowed to turn Bangladesh into a trillion-dollar, climate-resilient and sustainable economy overcoming all challenges, stressing that economic growth and environmental protection must go hand in hand.

“Bangladesh is on the frontline of climate change. Yet, our contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions is less than 0.5%. Despite these challenges, we remain committed to building a trillion-dollar, climate-resilient and sustainable economy,” he said while addressing the High-Level Segment of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye.

The Prime Minister also stressed that industrialisation and development must protect nature and maintain ecological balance.

He said Bangladesh had set a target of meeting 20 percent of its electricity needs from renewable sources by 2030 and was working to develop 4,000 megawatts of solar power with special tax incentives.

The government was also promoting waste-to-energy initiatives, green industries, environment-friendly transport, including electric vehicles, and products such as jute bags, Tarique said.

He said Bangladesh was developing a national framework for carbon trading as part of its efforts to promote a sustainable economy.

Highlighting the government's environmental initiatives, the Prime Minister said the country planned to plant 250 million trees over the next five years.

He also mentioned plans to excavate 20,000 kilometres of rivers and canals, alongside the Padma Barrage and Teesta Barrage Master Plan, to retain water, reduce flood risks, revive wetlands and recharge groundwater.

Bangladesh was also restoring mangroves on reclaimed coastal land to protect communities and strengthen climate resilience, Tarique added.

He stressed the need to ensure the participation of women and young people in climate action, create decent green jobs and reduce global emissions to keep the 1.5-degree Celsius goal within reach.

At the event, the Prime Minister outlined five urgent actions to address the needs of climate-vulnerable countries, including allocating at least 50 percent of international climate finance to adaptation and introducing debt-relief measures.

He expressed hope that COP31 would deliver meaningful, balanced and ambitious results, particularly for countries most vulnerable to climate change.

headline: PM outlines five actions to address needs of climate-vulnerable countries
brief:

body_html:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday outlined five urgent actions to address the needs of climate-vulnerable countries, including allocating at least 50 percent of international climate finance to adaptation and introducing debt-relief measures.

“Climate-vulnerable countries need grants, not more loans that increase their debt,” he said while addressing the High-Level Segment of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye.

Tarique also called for reliable financial support, access to modern technology and stronger assistance for adaptation, saying the global climate finance system remained inadequate and did not properly address the needs and priorities of developing countries.

Guided by the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities, the Prime Minister placed five proposals before the international community.

First, he called for allocating at least 50 percent of international climate finance to adaptation, based on each country's priorities, while continuing to support efforts to reduce emissions.

Second, Tarique urged the introduction of debt-relief measures, including Debt-for-Climate Swaps and Climate-Resilient Debt Clauses, for vulnerable countries.

Third, he called for fair access to climate-friendly technologies and support for their transfer to developing countries.

Fourth, the Prime Minister stressed the need to accelerate the shift to renewable energy through affordable financing, skills development and a fair energy transition.

Fifth, he urged world leaders to adopt the Belem-Antalya Action Mechanism for a just transition at COP31, with fair finance and fair trade at its heart.

Tarique said climate-related losses and damages were putting a heavy burden on economies, while rising debt payments and limited financial resources were making the situation more difficult.

He said Bangladesh was on the frontline of climate change, although its contribution to global greenhouse gas emissions was less than 0.5 percent.

Despite these challenges, Bangladesh remained committed to building a trillion-dollar, climate-resilient and sustainable economy, the Prime Minister added.

Guided by the philosophy of “Bangladesh Before All”, the government believed economic growth and environmental protection must go hand in hand, he said, stressing that industrialisation and development must protect nature and maintain ecological balance.

Tarique said Bangladesh had set a target of meeting 20 percent of its electricity needs from renewable sources by 2030 and was working to develop 4,000 megawatts of solar power with special tax incentives.

He said the government was also promoting waste-to-energy initiatives, green industries, electric vehicles and environment-friendly products such as jute bags, while developing a national framework for carbon trading.

The Prime Minister said the country planned to plant 250 million trees over five years.

He also highlighted plans to excavate 20,000 kilometres of rivers and canals, alongside the Padma Barrage and Teesta Barrage Master Plan, to retain water, reduce flood risks, revive wetlands and recharge groundwater.

Bangladesh was also restoring mangroves on reclaimed coastal land to protect communities and strengthen climate resilience, Tarique added.

He called for ensuring the participation of women and young people in climate action, creating decent green jobs and reducing global emissions to keep the 1.5-degree Celsius goal within reach.

The Prime Minister expressed hope that COP31 would deliver meaningful, balanced and ambitious results, particularly for countries most vulnerable to climate change. “Let us turn our commitments into action. Let us strengthen global solidarity and build a sustainable future together.”

Tarique arrived in Antalya on November 10 on a three-day visit to attend the UN Climate Change Conference.

headline: No evidence of petrol bomb use in fire at MP Nusrat’s  house: Home Minister
brief:
Investigators had so far found no evidence suggesting that petrol bombs were used to set fire to the village home of MP Nusrat Tabassum, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said on Thursday.
“An initial investigation
body_html:
Investigators had so far found no evidence suggesting that petrol bombs were used to set fire to the village home of MP Nusrat Tabassum, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said on Thursday.

“An initial investigation has found that electrical short circuit may have caused the incident,” he told Parliament as Opposition Chief Whip Nahid Islam alleged that fascist Awami League might have link behind this fire incident.

The Home Minister said investigators found no signs of a petrol bomb explosion on the walls of the house. “Nor had any witnesses provided information suggesting that petrol bombs were used in the incident,” he added.

He said the initial assessment by the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) indicated that the fire was more likely caused by an electrical fault, as the house had old and weak electrical wiring.

“An initial assessment suggests that the possibility of an electrical short circuit is quite high,” he said, adding that a photograph from the scene also appeared to indicate a possible short circuit.

The fire broke out at a tin-shed, semi-concrete house in the MP’s village, he said.

The house, which was unoccupied, was around 20 metres from a three-storey building where her parents live, he added.

Two goats kept at the house died in the fire and some shoemaking materials, clothes and other belongings were also inside, he added.

The minister said an additional superintendent of police and the officer-in-charge of the local police station had visited the scene.

He said he also spoke to the superintendent of police on Thursday morning and directed further investigation.

Fire service personnel from a neighbouring police station were brought in immediately after the incident was reported and managed to bring the blaze under control, the minister said.

Salahuddin said he had already ordered a joint investigation involving the BGB, Fire Service and Civil Defence, civil administration and police to establish whether the fire was accidental or the result of sabotage.

He said photographs, audio and video recordings, and other evidence collected from the scene had been preserved for examination.

A general diary (GD) has been filed with the police in connection with the incident.

The minister said the police were investigating the matter under GD No. 703, dated Thursday.Emphasising that the findings were still preliminary, he said a definitive conclusion could only be reached after the investigation was completed.

“If further investigation reveals that anyone was involved in sabotage, appropriate action will be taken,” he said.

Earlier, Opposition Chief Whip Md Nahid Islam expressed concern over the security of lawmakers and leaders of the July Uprising and anti-fascist movement following the reported arson attack on the ancestral home of NCP lawmaker Nusrat Tabassum in Daulatpur, Kushtia.

He said miscreants hurled four petrol bombs at the house around midnight on Wednesday, setting it on fire and killing cattle kept there.

He alleged that the Officer-in-Charge (OC) of the local police station had commented that no evidence of petrol bombs was found at the scene, although no forensic team had visited the spot until Thursday noon.

"Without any forensic investigation, how can the OC conclude that no petrol bombs were used? I do not know how a police officer can make such a comment," he said.

Citing that the fallen fascist force started anarchy and carrying out sabotages across the country, NCP lawmaker Nahid Islam said it is evident that they are the prime targets, while BNP are the second targets for the fascist forces.

He also referred to an attack on Hasib Al Islam, a coordinator of the Anti-Discrimination Student Movement, in Moulvibazar two days earlier, alleging that no one had been arrested even after 48 hours.

Citing Mentioning reported petrol bomb and crude bomb explosions in different parts of the country, including inside Dhaka University, he questioned the government's response to the deteriorating security situation.

"Even after setting fire to the house of a sitting MP, can’t we still call it a deterioration in law and order? This is the question," he said.

He said the attacks had created fear among lawmakers, leaders of the July Uprising and activists of the anti-fascist movement over their personal security and that of their families.

The lawmaker also sought a clear response from the government over what he described as the government’s compromising attitude towards the Awami League and the question of bringing the fascist forces to justice.

headline: PM seeks UK support for Rohingya repatriation, climate finance
brief:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday sought stronger British diplomatic support for the safe, voluntary and dignified repatriation of Rohingyas sheltered in Bangladesh to their homeland in Myanmar.
He made the request during a me
body_html:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday sought stronger British diplomatic support for the safe, voluntary and dignified repatriation of Rohingyas sheltered in Bangladesh to their homeland in Myanmar.

He made the request during a meeting with British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on the sidelines of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.

He said the two sides discussed Rohingya repatriation, support for Bangladesh's climate adaptation efforts, migration, stronger economic ties and other issues of mutual interest.

During the meeting, Tarique stressed the need to intensify international diplomatic efforts to find a sustainable solution to the Rohingya crisis.

He said Bangladesh was seeking a more active diplomatic role from the United Kingdom to ensure the safe, voluntary and dignified return of the Rohingyas to Myanmar.

The Prime Minister pointed out that Bangladesh was a densely populated country and had been hosting a large number of Rohingyas for nearly a decade, putting considerable pressure on its economy, society, culture and environment.

He also noted that the prolonged presence of the Rohingyas could affect livelihood opportunities for local communities and pose risks to regional security.

The meeting also emphasised the need to further strengthen cooperation between Bangladesh and the UK in climate action, addressing humanitarian crises, migration and economic partnership.

headline: PM seeks increased Australian investment, support for Rohingya repatriation
brief:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday sought increased Australian investment in Bangladesh and its support in ensuring the safe repatriation of Rohingyas to their homeland in Myanmar.
He made the requests during a b
body_html:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday sought increased Australian investment in Bangladesh and its support in ensuring the safe repatriation of Rohingyas to their homeland in Myanmar.

He made the requests during a bilateral meeting with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on the sidelines of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, held at 10:30am local time, said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.

He said the two leaders discussed climate change, investment opportunities in Bangladesh, the Rohingya crisis and other issues of mutual interest.

During the meeting, Tarique invited Albanese to visit Bangladesh. In response, the Australian Prime Minister expressed hope that he would be able to visit the country at a convenient time next year.

Albanese also invited Tarique to visit Australia, and the Bangladesh Prime Minister expressed hope that he would make the visit at a convenient time.

During the discussions on climate change, Tarique stressed the need to give priority to the needs of developing countries, particularly those most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change.

He appreciated Australia's leadership role in the ongoing COP31 negotiation process, saying Bangladesh was among the countries most vulnerable to the adverse impacts of climate change.

On investment, the Prime Minister highlighted the opportunities available in Bangladesh and called for increased Australian investment in the country.

The two leaders also discussed cooperation in the agriculture sector.

On the Rohingya issue, Tarique sought Australia's support for ensuring the safe repatriation of Myanmar’s displaced nationals sheltered in Bangladesh to their homeland.

He called for stronger Australian diplomatic efforts to help resolve the crisis, stressing that it originated in Myanmar and that a lasting solution must also be found there.

The Prime Minister also briefed Albanese on Bangladesh's plans for renewable energy, saying the government was working to meet 20 percent of the country's total electricity demand from renewable sources by 2030.

He also highlighted various government initiatives to protect the environment and address the impacts of climate change, including a plan to plant 25 crore trees across the country and programmes for excavating canals.

headline: Govt approves direct LNG procurement from four foreign suppliers
brief:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on Thursday approved for the direct procurement of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from four international suppliers including Japan’s JERA Global Markets Pte Ltd to meet the country’s energy demand.
The committee also approved pol
body_html:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs on Thursday approved for the direct procurement of liquefied natural gas (LNG) from four international suppliers including Japan’s JERA Global Markets Pte Ltd to meet the country’s energy demand.

The committee also approved policy for reducing the tender submission period for the purchase of 6,200 tonnes of dates for the holy month of Ramadan in 2027 and for installing mobile network coverage at the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.

Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury presided over the meeting held at the Secretariat.

The committee recommended policy approval for purchasing LNG directly from JERA Global Markets Pte Ltd (JERAGM) of Japan under Section 68 of the Public Procurement Act, 2006 and Rule 99(2) of the Public Procurement Rules, 2025.

The proposal also includes signing the finalised format of the short-term LNG Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) and term sheet between Petrobangla and JERAGM.

The committee separately recommended policy approval for direct procurement of LNG from ADNOC Trading Ltd of the UAE under the same legal provisions.

It also recommended direct procurement of LNG from Ojimadu & Marites Oil Marketing Nigeria Ltd and Uzzy Gems Beehive.

The Energy and Mineral Resources Division placed all three LNG procurement proposals.

In another decision, the committee recommended reducing the time allowed for preparing and submitting tenders for the purchase of 6,200 metric tonnes of dates through international open tender for Ramadan 2027.

The Commerce Ministry placed the proposal under Rule 102(1) (a) of the Public Procurement Rules, 2025, citing the state’s urgent requirements.

The committee also approved policy approval for following the direct procurement method to install mobile network coverage at the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport under the project titled “Installation of Mobile Network at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport Third Terminal”.

The Posts and Telecommunications Division placed the proposal.

brief:

The luncheon was held at Regnu
body_html:
Dr Zubaida Rahman, the wife of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, on Thursday attended a luncheon hosted by Turkish First Lady Emine Erdoğan.

The luncheon was held at Regnum Hotel in Antalya, Türkiye, in honour of the spouses of heads of state and government and other distinguished guests attending the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), said PM's Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.

Emine Erdoğan warmly welcomed Zubaida at the event. They also exchanged greetings and held a cordial conversation.

headline: Global climate efforts stalled for five years, stronger targets needed: report
brief:

The assessment came during a UN
body_html:
Global efforts to combat climate change have made little progress over the past five years, as unfulfilled commitments and cancelled-out initiatives have prevented the world from slowing the pace of global warming, a report said Thursday.

The assessment came during a UN climate conference in Antalya, Türkiye, where world leaders were scheduled to deliver further statements on the worsening climate crisis and their plans to address it.

According to an independent report by Climate Action Tracker, collective climate action has effectively stalled for five consecutive years, with positive and negative measures offsetting each other.

During the first five years after the 2015 Paris Agreement, global climate initiatives reduced projected warming by a full degree Celsius (1.8 degrees Fahrenheit). However, the situation has remained unchanged since then, the report said.

Climate change is primarily driven by greenhouse gas emissions released through the burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas. Tackling the crisis requires substantial annual reductions in emissions. Countries outline their individual commitments to cut emissions through nationally determined contributions (NDCs), with the pace and methods varying from one country to another.

As collective efforts have failed to significantly reduce global emissions, the world is now heading towards an irreversible breach of the 1.5-degree Celsius (2.7-degree Fahrenheit) warming threshold above pre-industrial levels set under the Paris Agreement, the report warned.

Even if all countries fulfil their existing climate commitments, the global temperature is projected to rise by 2.6 degrees Celsius (4.7 degrees Fahrenheit) by the end of this century.

That projection remains unchanged from 2024 and 2025, indicating that the latest round of commitments made last year has failed to significantly alter the expected warming trajectory, said Sarah Heck, a climate policy analyst at Climate Analytics and lead author of the report.

"This is still not enough," Heck said, stressing that countries need to strengthen their climate targets.

Leaders of island nations delivered a similar message to the international community on Wednesday, with more expected to reiterate their concerns on Thursday.

Although climate change is intensifying storms, heatwaves, droughts and floods worldwide, island nations face an additional existential threat as rising sea levels gradually swallow their territories.

"Every new oil well drilled, every piece of coal extracted is a threat to my country's future. The discovery of new fossil fuel resources is not something to celebrate, but something to fear," Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said on Wednesday.

She was joined in raising concerns by leaders from Tuvalu, the Bahamas, Antigua and Barbuda, Niue and other island nations, who were expected to make similar appeals.

"No one has the right to pollute their neighbors," Heine said, urging the world to wake up to the climate crisis.

Recalling how coral reefs she had seen this year had turned from "bright and lush" to white due to bleaching, she warned that the global response to the inevitable breach of the 1.5-degree warming limit must be overwhelming or the world as people know it would be lost.

Meanwhile, Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley said wealthy countries must move beyond making financial promises and provide more funding to poorer nations to help them recover from climate-related damage and adapt to rising temperatures.

"Pledges are not payments. But even the promised pledges are now 70% below previous levels," Mottley told fellow leaders on Wednesday.

She added that applause and expressions of support at international meetings had never rebuilt a single home in any country.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s wife Dr Zubaida Rahman on Wednesday called for stronger global cooperation, affordable climate finance and technology transfer to achieve zero waste, saying waste should be turned into resources, clean energy and opportunities for growth.

“Waste should not be wasted without any use. It should become a resource, a source of energy, and an opportunity for growth,” she said while addressing a high-level meeting of spouses of world leaders on the Global Zero Waste Alliance on the sidelines of the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye.

The meeting was convened by Turkish First Lady Emine Erdoğan, whom Zubaida thanked for her leadership in promoting the zero-waste agenda.

She said Bangladesh strongly supported the Global Zero Waste Alliance, which is aligned with the government's vision of a cleaner environment, healthier communities and a sustainable future.

Zubaida said the government's 3R strategy promotes waste reduction, reuse and recycling, while the Solid Waste Management Rules strengthen waste segregation and safe disposal.

Under its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0), Bangladesh aims to reduce 1.78 million tonnes of CO₂ equivalent emissions from the waste sector by 2035, she said.

The Prime Minister’s wife said the country's priorities include recycling, composting, landfill-gas recovery, waste-to-energy projects, improved wastewater treatment and the safe management of medical and healthcare waste.

Highlighting a major initiative in the capital, she said a waste-to-energy project was being developed in Dhaka to process 3,000 tonnes of household waste every day and generate 42.5 megawatts of electricity.

“We want to expand such projects to major cities across Bangladesh,” Zubaida said, adding that the goal was to turn urban waste into clean energy while protecting the environment.

She also said the government was working to clean lakes, canals, ponds and wetlands to reduce plastic pollution.

headline: World leaders begin COP31 talks amid concerns over inadequate climate action
brief:
World leaders are set to begin formal discussions Wednesday at the United Nations climate change conference in Turkey, seeking concrete measures to tackle global warming amid growing concerns that efforts to address the crisis remain inadequate and too slow.
However, the...
body_html:
World leaders are set to begin formal discussions Wednesday at the United Nations climate change conference in Turkey, seeking concrete measures to tackle global warming amid growing concerns that efforts to address the crisis remain inadequate and too slow.

However, the extent of progress that can be achieved at the Conference of the Parties, known as COP31, remains uncertain, with previous climate summits facing criticism over unfulfilled commitments and limited results.

At the 2023 conference in Dubai, delegates agreed to move away from fossil fuels, including coal, oil and gas, which are the main drivers of climate change. But subsequent conferences in Azerbaijan and Brazil failed to reach significant agreements on emissions reductions.

Last year's conference in Brazil ended with a compromise deal that pledged additional financial support to help climate-vulnerable countries adapt to the impacts of climate change.

This year's conference, hosted by Turkey with Australia leading the negotiations, officially opened on Monday amid mounting concerns that global efforts are falling short of what is needed to address the climate crisis.

Scientists warn that global temperatures are likely to exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) above pre-industrial levels recorded in the early 1800s. Keeping the rise within this limit was a key objective of the 2015 Paris Agreement and has remained central to international climate negotiations.

The discussions are also taking place against the backdrop of the war in Iran, which has driven up global prices of gasoline, oil and petroleum-based products, including fertilizers and pesticides. The price increases have prompted governments to reconsider their energy policies and investments in renewable sources such as wind and solar power.

"We don't need more promises, we need plans," said John Kerry, former US secretary of state and presidential climate envoy.

However, the United States, the world's second-largest polluter after China, is notably absent from the conference for the second consecutive year.

US President Donald Trump, who has dismissed climate change as a hoax, has targeted offshore wind energy projects and rolled back regulations aimed at limiting emissions from power plants.

headline: Police HQ's recommendation to revoke former Gazipur commissioner's suspension overlooked for eight months
brief:
Despite a recommendation from Police Headquarters to withdraw the suspension of former Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP) Commissioner Md Nazmul Karim Khan, the Home Ministry has yet to take any decision in this regard, even after eight months.
Sources at the Police Headq...
body_html:
Despite a recommendation from Police Headquarters to withdraw the suspension of former Gazipur Metropolitan Police (GMP) Commissioner Md Nazmul Karim Khan, the Home Ministry has yet to take any decision in this regard, even after eight months.

Sources at the Police Headquarters said in a significant development concerning the suspension, the Police Headquarters had recommended withdrawing it back on March 2 in a letter to the Home Ministry, saying it had no documents or information about the allegations against him or the grounds for the punitive action.

The recommendation has raised questions about the basis on which a serving DIG was sent away from his post and subsequently placed under suspension by the Home Ministry, apart from the last eight months in which the recommendation to withdraw the suspension has been ignored.

In a letter sent to the Home Ministry on March 2, 2026, the Police Headquarters said it had no relevant documents regarding a report allegedly submitted by the then Inspector General of Police (IGP) to the ministry against Nazmul Karim Khan.

The letter, signed by then Additional DIG (Personnel Management-1) Khandaker Shamima Yasmin, said the then IGP had sent a report to the Home Ministry on October 20, 2025, under IGP Diary No.488.

However, the Police Headquarters said no documents relating to the matter were preserved there.

It further stated that no inquiry had been conducted into the allegations mentioned in the two instances referred to in the correspondence, as the headquarters had no information or supporting documents regarding them.

The letter also said the concerned officer (DIG Nazmul Karim Khan)  had not been informed of the circumstances leading to the officer's suspension and the Police Headquarters had no relevant information on record.

In view of these circumstances, the headquarters recommended withdrawal of Nazmul Karim Khan's suspension, according to the letter sent in response to a Home Ministry communication dated March 1, 2026.

Earlier, on September 1, 2025, the Police Headquarters issued an order directing Nazmul Karim Khan to report to its headquarters the following day. He was also instructed to hand over charge of the Gazipur Metropolitan Police to the next senior officer.

The order was signed by Mohammad Sharif Uddin, then Additional DIG (Headquarters).

Subsequently, on November 10, 2025, the Home Ministry issued a notification placing Nazmul Karim Khan under temporary suspension and attaching him to the ministry.

The notification, signed by Senior Secretary Nasimul Gani on behalf of the President, stated that it was necessary and appropriate in the public interest to keep him away from government service.

Invoking Section 39(1) of the Government Service Act, 2018, the ministry ordered his temporary suspension and attachment to the Home Ministry. He was also entitled to subsistence allowance in accordance with the applicable rules during the suspension period, the notification said.

Nazmul Karim Khan assumed office as GMP Commissioner on November 12, 2024, and remained in the position until September 2, 2025, according to his personal service record.

headline: Bumper early Aman harvest brings little cheer to Thakurgaon farmers
brief:
The fields across Thakurgaon are turning golden as farmers harvest early varieties of Aman rice, but the bumper yield has failed to bring them the expected relief.
Despite a good harvest this sea
body_html:
The fields across Thakurgaon are turning golden as farmers harvest early varieties of Aman rice, but the bumper yield has failed to bring them the expected relief.

Despite a good harvest this season, growers are struggling to get fair prices for their paddy, raising fears that higher production will not translate into higher profits.

With harvesting and threshing activities gaining momentum across the district, many farmers are finding that the market price barely covers their production costs, which have increased due to higher prices of fuel, pesticides and agricultural labour.

A visit to different parts of the district found farmers busy harvesting, carrying paddy home and threshing the crop.

While the fields are witnessing a productive season, the mood among growers remains subdued over falling market prices.

Jamal Uddin, a farmer from Bhaulahat area of Sadar upazila, said he cultivated early Aman on six bighas of land and had initially been delighted with the yield.

“I am now harvesting the crop and bringing it home. The yield is very good, which made me happy at first. But looking at the market price, I am no longer optimistic. After meeting the production costs, there will hardly be any profit,” he said.

Another farmer, Mohsin, said the price of a sack containing two maunds of paddy had fallen from Tk 2,200–2,250 at the beginning of the season to around Tk 2,100.

He said paddy was currently selling for around Tk 1,050–1,100 per maund, while farmers would need Tk 1,200–1,300 per maund to get a reasonable return.

“If the price were Tk 1,200–1,300 per maund, we could sell a two-maund sack for Tk 2,400–2,600. Now the price of paddy is almost equal to the production cost. The only thing left for us to earn something from is the straw,” he said.

Production rises, returns remain uncertain

According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), Aman cultivation in Thakurgaon exceeded the season’s target.

The district had set a cultivation target of 137,270 hectares, but farmers cultivated 137,300 hectares, exceeding the target by 30 hectares.

Harvesting of early varieties has already begun in different parts of the district, with paddy from around 15,000 hectares harvested so far.

The high-yielding varieties grown in the district include BRRI Dhan-75, BRRI Dhan-90, BRRI Dhan-17 and BRRI Dhan-7. Farmers have also started harvesting hybrid varieties, including Dhanigold.

However, the prospect of a bumper harvest has been overshadowed by concerns over weak farmgate prices and the rising cost of cultivation.

Concerns have also been raised over the influence of millers and traders in the local paddy market.

The absence of government procurement at the beginning of the harvesting season has further limited farmers’ bargaining power, leaving many dependent on local traders.

Government procurement yet to begin

DAE Deputy Director Majedul Islam, however, described early Aman harvesting as a positive development for farmers, particularly during the lean period in the northern region.

“Early harvesting is a blessing for farmers. Kartik is traditionally considered a difficult period for people in this region, as there used to be little agricultural activity at this time. But with the introduction of different early-maturing varieties, farmers can now bring Aman rice home ahead of the usual season,” he said.

He acknowledged that farmers were getting somewhat lower prices but said they could also earn from selling paddy straw, which fetches a relatively good price during this period due to demand for cattle feed.

He said the government had not yet started its Aman procurement drive and farmers would have to wait for it to begin.

District Assistant Agricultural Marketing Officer Sakhawat Hossain also acknowledged that farmers were not getting fair prices despite the arrival of early Aman paddy in the market.

“We are advising farmers not to sell their paddy immediately at low prices. They can store it at home for some time and sell it later after analysing the market to get a better price,” he said.

He added that the Department of Agricultural Marketing was regularly monitoring local markets to prevent unscrupulous traders or groups from purchasing paddy at low prices and hoarding it to manipulate the market.

“If the price were Tk 1,200–1,300 per maund, we could sell a two-maund sack for Tk 2,400–2,600. Now the price of paddy is almost equal to the production cost. The only thing left for us to earn something from is the straw,” he said.

Production rises, returns remain uncertain

According to the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE), Aman cultivation in Thakurgaon exceeded the season’s target.

The district had set a cultivation target of 137,270 hectares, but farmers cultivated 137,300 hectares, exceeding the target by 30 hectares.

The high-yielding varieties grown in the district include BRRI Dhan-75, BRRI Dhan-90, BRRI Dhan-17 and BRRI Dhan-7. Farmers have also started harvesting hybrid varieties, including Dhanigold.

However, the prospect of a bumper harvest has been overshadowed by concerns over weak farmgate prices and the rising cost of cultivation.

Concerns have also been raised over the influence of millers and traders in the local paddy market.

The absence of government procurement at the beginning of the harvesting season has further limited farmers’ bargaining power, leaving many dependent on local traders.

Government procurement yet to begin

DAE Deputy Director Majedul Islam, however, described early Aman harvesting as a positive development for farmers, particularly during the lean period in the northern region.

“Early harvesting is a blessing for farmers. Kartik is traditionally considered a difficult period for people in this region, as there used to be little agricultural activity at this time. But with the introduction of different early-maturing varieties, farmers can now bring Aman rice home ahead of the usual season,” he said.

He acknowledged that farmers were getting somewhat lower prices but said they could also earn from selling paddy straw, which fetches a relatively good price during this period due to demand for cattle feed.

He said the government had not yet started its Aman procurement drive and farmers would have to wait for it to begin.

District Assistant Agricultural Marketing Officer Sakhawat Hossain also acknowledged that farmers were not getting fair prices despite the arrival of early Aman paddy in the market.

“We are advising farmers not to sell their paddy immediately at low prices. They can store it at home for some time and sell it later after analysing the market to get a better price,” he said.

He added that the Department of Agricultural Marketing was regularly monitoring local markets to prevent unscrupulous traders or groups from purchasing paddy at low prices and hoarding it to manipulate the market.

headline: BNP on high alert to thwart AL attempts to create unrest centring Hasina's return
brief: What the month of December holds has been a major topic of discussion in the country's politics over the past several months, ever since ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who has now spent over two years in India, announced her intention to return to Bangladesh ...
body_html:
What the month of December holds has been a major topic of discussion in the country's politics over the past several months, ever since ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina, who has now spent over two years in India, announced her intention to return to Bangladesh that month.

Leaders and activists of the Awami League, which remains under a ban on its activities, have been energised by Hasina's announcement, and they have been campaigning on social media, as well as through their foreign networks, to prepare the grounds for her return, which remains uncertain.

The ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) believes the Awami League’s underground network is trying to stoke unrest across the country in anticipation of welcoming back their leader, with government sources saying the party is planning subversive activities.

The BNP has stepped up organisational activities, mobilised its grassroots leaders and activists, and sought to mend ties with former allies. It has also instructed its leaders and workers to remain alert, avoid provocation and report suspicious activities to the administration rather than take the law into their own hands.

The party and its affiliated organisations, including Jubo Dal, Chhatra Dal (JCD) and Sramik Dal, are active on the ground. Law enforcement agencies suspect AL activists were involved in recent garment workers’ protests, cocktail explosions and vehicle arson in Dhaka and other parts of the country.

At a BNP parliamentary party meeting chaired by Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman at parliament premises on Monday, “The message is loud and clear: we are on the streets, and we must remain on the streets. All conspiracies must be confronted on the streets,” Tarique told the meeting.

Meanwhile, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said the government would use the Bangladesh-India extradition treaty to bring Hasina back.

The home minister assured parliament that no conspiracy, whether hatched inside or outside the country, would be allowed to revive fascism.

“I want to assure the people of the country that no conspiracy or blueprint, whether hatched within the country, beyond the border or through a combination of forces, will be allowed to be implemented here,” he said.

Referring to a cocktail explosion on the roof of a car near the Dhaka University Business Faculty building, Salahuddin said such an incident did not mean that the country's law and order situation had deteriorated. It was not reasonable, he said, to describe the overall situation as extremely alarming based on a few symbolic incidents.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kabir said Hasina could not return on a new passport and that her return would have to follow the legal process under the extradition treaty.

Political analysts say the BNP faces the challenge of rebuilding its organisational structure while running the government. After being out of power for a long time, some leaders are now occupied with government and administrative responsibilities. Competition for local leadership, dissatisfaction over committee positions and concerns about discipline have also emerged.

The party is preparing for its national council and reorganising its central committee, standing committee, advisory council and affiliate organisations. New committees have recently been announced for BNP's Dhaka North and South units and Jubo Dal's Dhaka North unit. Reorganisation of Chhatra Dal, Jubo Dal and Swechchhasebak Dal is also underway.

BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi said people would never accept Hasina's return in the way AL leaders were claiming.

“Will she suddenly descend by parachute and everyone will welcome her by beating drums? Can that ever happen? The soil of Bengal is the soil of heroes. This land has given birth to many heroes. Those who flee the country after shedding the blood of their own people cannot simply fly back and take over. That is never possible. The people themselves will resist Hasina,” he said.

“In that roar, neither Sheikh Hasina nor even her patrons and their grandfathers will be able to do anything,” Rizvi added, saying people always resist injustice.

“The streets and the field of movements have not been given to anyone as hereditary property, allowing you to provoke us one after another while we sit silently,” he said.

“You can see that cocktails and bombs are being exploded from inside alleys in some places. Instructions are reportedly coming from a neighbouring country. The people will resist them appropriately. The government is always prepared in this regard,” he said.

BNP standing committee member Amanullah Aman said the public would not accept attempts to create unrest through a few cocktail explosions. Anti-fascist political parties would jointly resist any move to bring back the ousted autocrat, he said.

“She can come, let her come. The people of Bangladesh are also prepared,” Aman said.

State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Nurul Haque Nur, also the president of  Gono Odhikar Parishad, which is a BNP ally, described the talk of Hasina's return in December as ridiculous, alleging that hostile foreign forces were using fascist elements to create instability in Bangladesh.

BNP National Executive Committee member Mamun Hasan said the party would remain active on the ground but would not allow disorder. It would cooperate with the government and administration to maintain peace and resist anyone attempting to create unrest.

“As the party in government, we will do whatever is necessary to cooperate with the administration if such cooperation is needed,” he told UNB.

Another BNP National Executive Committee member, Akramul Hasan, said the party would organise resistance against any terrorist activities. He said the AL should seek forgiveness first from the people if it wanted to return to politics.

He said cocktail explosions might create some fear in a city as large as Dhaka but would have no meaningful political impact. Referring to the AL's past record of arson, deaths, corruption, looting, misrule, crossfire and enforced disappearances, he said isolated acts of violence would not win public support.

JCD President Rakibul Islam Rakib said attempts to create disorder in the country are worsening the situation for AL's jailed leaders and activists, he said.

Dismissing the December return claims, Rakib said Bangladesh would celebrate the month of victory in the Liberation War in the grandest manner since 1971. Chhatra Dal will organise Victory celebrations at educational institutions across the country from December 1.

Meanwhile, the BNP is taking initiatives to reduce some of the distance that has opened up between itself and its allies. Some partner parties have expressed dissatisfaction over political assessments after the formation of the government, pre-election commitments and the pace of state reforms.

The BNP plans to hold meetings with its partners in late November or early December. Discussions may also take place with Tarique Rahman on the party's 31-point reform proposal, the July Charter, constitutional amendments, local government elections and future political programmes.

headline: COP31: Tarique takes part in World Leaders’ Summit
brief:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman joined the World Leaders’ Summit of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Exhibition Centre in Antalya, Türkiye, on Wednesday afternoon.
He joined the summit around 12:
body_html:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman joined the World Leaders’ Summit of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) at the Antalya Exhibition Centre in Antalya, Türkiye, on Wednesday afternoon.

He joined the summit around 12:15pm local time, said PM’s Deputy Press Secretary Hasan Shiplu.

More than 150 heads of state and government are taking part in the two-day summit, which will end on Thursday, he said.

The Prime Minister was accompanied by his wife, Dr Zubaida Rahman, Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo and State Minister-1 for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir.

Tarique reached the conference venue at 10:10am local time, where he was welcomed by the organisers.

Before the opening session, he exchanged greetings and pleasantries with heads of state and government and senior representatives of international organisations at the Leaders’ Lounge.

He also held brief, informal conversations with world leaders on issues of mutual interest.

After the World Leaders’ Summit, Tarique is scheduled to attend a Zero Waste Roundtable meeting in the afternoon.

On the sidelines of the conference, the Prime Minister is also scheduled to hold separate meetings with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, Shiplu said.

In the evening, he will attend a dinner hosted by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in honour of world leaders.

The Prime Minister arrived in Antalya on Tuesday to attend the conference.

World leaders are expected to discuss concrete measures to tackle global warming amid growing concerns that international efforts to address the climate crisis remain inadequate and too slow.

The conference, hosted by Türkiye with Australia leading the negotiations, officially opened on Monday and will run through November 20.

The discussions are also taking place amid the war in Iran, which has pushed up global prices of fuel and petroleum-based products, including fertilisers and pesticides.

The price hikes have prompted governments to reconsider their energy policies and investment in renewable sources such as wind and solar power.

headline: Bangladesh Bank issues revamped Tk 1,500cr refinance scheme for financial inclusion
brief:
Bangladesh Bank has issued a comprehensive, unified policy revamping its Tk 1,500 crore refinance scheme aimed at bolstering financial inclusion for marginal farmers, low-income professionals, small business owners, students, and remittance-recipient families.
The revamp...
body_html:
Bangladesh Bank has issued a comprehensive, unified policy revamping its Tk 1,500 crore refinance scheme aimed at bolstering financial inclusion for marginal farmers, low-income professionals, small business owners, students, and remittance-recipient families.

The revamped guidelines, issued by the central bank's Financial Inclusion Department (FID) on November 12, 2026, replace all previous circulars and letters concerning the fund, including FID Circular-01/2021. The scheme will operate on a revolving basis for the next five years, backed by Bangladesh Bank's own funds.

Target Beneficiaries: Marginal and landless farmers, micro and small entrepreneurs, traditional professionals (such as fishermen, cobblers, goldsmiths, barbers, potters, blacksmiths, and tailors), small traders, low-income earners in coastal and haor areas, ethnic minorities, and differently-abled individuals will receive priority.

Women Empowerment: At least 25 percent of the total loans under this scheme must be disbursed to female borrowers and entrepreneurs.

Farmer Smart Cards: Marginal and landless farmers holding "Farmer Smart Cards" under the Department of Agricultural Extension will receive priority in loan acquisition, though cardless farmers will not be excluded.

Student Banking: Under the student banking component, banks can extend loans with parental repayment guarantees for vocational or IT training, income-generating activities for students post-18, and higher education expenses (such as medical, engineering, and MBA programs) for underprivileged students up to the age of 25.

Individual and Group Caps: Commercial banks can provide individual loans up to Tk 10 lakh. For group-based loans (2–5 members), the limit is set at up to Tk 8 lakh per group (Tk 2 lakh per member), capped at Tk 40 lakh total.

Interest Rates: Participating banks will secure refinancing from Bangladesh Bank at an annual rate of 1.0 percent, while the maximum interest rate for end-borrowers is capped at 7.0 percent on a declining balance basis.

Collateral: No security collateral can be demanded for loans up to Tk 5 lakh, though personal guarantees from up to two individuals alongside the borrower are permissible. Loans exceeding Tk 5 lakh may require reasonable collateral based on banker-customer relations.

Loans under the scheme carry a maximum grace period of 6 months, with a total repayment tenor of up to 5 years (60 months). Banks can disburse funds through their branches, sub-branches, agent banking, mobile financial services (MFS), and online platforms without imposing any extra processing fees beyond Bangladesh Bank's Schedule of Charges.

The central bank expects that this streamlined framework will significantly expand credit flow to underprivileged and productive sectors, driving grassroots economic growth and employment generation.

headline: COP31: Will Bangladesh's expectations be met through concrete climate financing or mere promises?
brief:
As climate-vulnerable Bangladesh seeks grants, technology transfer and financial support to tackle the growing impacts of climate change at COP31 in Antalya, the biggest challenge remains turning international promises into tangible assistance.
Wit
body_html:
As climate-vulnerable Bangladesh seeks grants, technology transfer and financial support to tackle the growing impacts of climate change at COP31 in Antalya, the biggest challenge remains turning international promises into tangible assistance.

With adaptation costs rising and the country facing mounting threats from cyclones, floods, salinity and rising sea levels, the summit has once again put the question of climate justice and equitable financing at the centre of Bangladesh's diplomatic agenda.

But whether this year's negotiations will deliver real financial commitments rather than another round of pledges remains uncertain.

As the global climate negotiations continue, a key question remains: will the longstanding demands of vulnerable countries like Bangladesh translate into concrete financial support, or will they remain confined to declarations and promises, as in previous climate summits?

Experts say Bangladesh's major priorities at COP31 should include securing grants instead of loan-based financing, ensuring easier access to adaptation funds, obtaining technological assistance and securing adequate funding to address climate-induced losses and damage.

They also stress the need for stronger diplomatic engagement and coordinated positions with other least developed countries (LDCs) and climate-vulnerable nations to strengthen Bangladesh's bargaining position.

Diplomatic engagement crucial to securing Bangladesh's demands

The effectiveness of Bangladesh's position at COP31 will largely depend on its diplomatic capacity and coordination with international alliances, experts say.

Professor Ainun Nishat said negotiations at COP summits primarily take place at the state level, with two separate spaces playing different roles.

The Blue Zone is where heads of state and government representatives discuss and negotiate the Paris Agreement and global climate policies, while the Green Zone provides a platform for civil society, NGOs and other organisations to present their demands and positions.

He said the main decision-making authority rests with government representatives. Therefore, diplomatic engagement by the head of government, environment minister, secretaries and relevant officials is crucial to advancing Bangladesh's interests.

He also stressed the importance of using bilateral meetings to raise issues relating to climate financing and the challenges faced by vulnerable countries.

Dr Atiq Rahman, meanwhile, said Bangladesh should not focus solely on its national interests but also highlight the collective demands of LDCs and other climate-vulnerable countries.

A united position in international negotiations could strengthen Bangladesh's efforts to secure its demands, he said.

Climate financing: Actual disbursement matters more than promises

Bangladesh needs substantial financial resources to address climate adaptation and climate-induced losses and damage. However, despite international pledges, significant challenges remain in securing actual disbursements, accessing funds on favourable terms and implementing projects.

M A Hasan of the Coast Foundation said international climate negotiations frequently feature announcements of large financial commitments, but their success cannot be measured merely by the amounts pledged.

He said it was important to determine who would provide the money, where it would come from, when it would be disbursed, under what conditions it would be provided, who would receive it and what tangible changes it would bring.

"Countries of the Global South are not asking for charity; they are demanding climate justice," he said.

Countries that have contributed the least to the climate crisis should not be forced to take on additional debt to protect their populations, he said, adding that financing arrangements that increase national debt or prioritise lenders' interests over people's needs are unacceptable.

The issue is particularly significant for Bangladesh, as taking on additional loans to address climate impacts could further increase economic pressure on the country.

Securing grant-based international climate assistance has therefore become a major priority.

International politics and financing challenges

Professor AKM Saiful Islam of the Institute of Water and Flood Management at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) said international politics had emerged as a major obstacle to climate financing and emissions reduction.

He said the United States' withdrawal from the Paris Agreement, global conflicts and the positions of oil-rich countries had complicated international climate cooperation and financing.

According to him, key issues at this year's summit include adaptation financing, direct grants and technological support to address losses and damage, implementation of international climate finance targets and a just transition in the energy sector.

He also highlighted the challenge of delivering on the climate finance commitments of $300 billion annually by 2035 and a longer-term target of $1.3 trillion.

Experts say securing climate financing will remain difficult amid the prevailing global political and economic uncertainties.

Bangladesh will therefore need to intensify bilateral and multilateral diplomatic efforts while pressing developed countries to fulfil their responsibilities.

Just transition and Bangladesh's domestic initiatives

Alongside international financing, Bangladesh's domestic environmental and energy policies could also shape its position at COP31.

Dr Saimum Parvez said the Prime Minister's participation in the summit reflected Bangladesh's commitment to environmental protection and climate action.

He said ensuring a just transition in the energy sector was one of the country's key priorities at the summit.

The government wants to move from a fossil fuel-dependent economy towards one based on renewable energy while protecting the livelihoods and employment of existing workers and creating new green jobs, he said.

He said the government had undertaken major programmes, including planting 250 million trees and excavating and re-excavating 20,000 kilometres of canals over the next five years.

Other priorities include renewable energy development, waste management, methane emission reduction and the promotion of environmentally friendly industries.

Highlighting Bangladesh's experience in climate adaptation, he said the country had made considerable progress in disaster preparedness through early warning systems for cyclones and floods, active volunteer networks, salt-tolerant crops and floating agriculture.

These initiatives could serve as examples for other climate-vulnerable countries, he added.

Paris Agreement goals remain a major challenge

The Paris Agreement, adopted at COP21 in 2015, aims to keep the rise in global temperatures well below 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels while pursuing efforts to limit the increase to 1.5 degrees Celsius.

However, a decade after its adoption, progress towards achieving these targets has remained insufficient.

Dependence on fossil fuels, inadequate investment, disagreements between developed and developing countries and shortages in climate financing have further complicated the situation.

Floods, cyclones, wildfires, droughts and heatwaves are intensifying in different parts of the world. Meanwhile, conflicts, energy security concerns and geopolitical instability are making international climate cooperation increasingly difficult.

For Bangladesh, the situation is particularly concerning, as climate change continues to threaten coastal communities, agriculture, livelihoods, water resources and food security.

Consequently, effective international cooperation on adaptation and addressing losses and damage remains essential alongside efforts to limit global temperature rises.

What can Bangladesh expect from COP31?

Bangladesh's demands at climate summits are not new. At previous conferences, the country repeatedly highlighted adaptation, loss and damage, technology transfer and climate financing.

However, a significant gap remains between international commitments and actual financial support.

At last year's COP30 in Belem, Brazil, Bangladesh did not secure any significant country-specific financial commitment or major visible achievement, according to the report.

Against this backdrop, actual disbursement of funds, simplified access to financing and guarantees for implementation have become more important than fresh declarations or pledges at COP31.

He also stressed the importance of using bilateral meetings to raise issues relating to climate financing and the challenges faced by vulnerable countries.

Judge of the Rajshahi Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court-2 Rezaul Karim handed down the verdict.

The convict is Limon Mia, hailing from Phulchari upazila in Gaibandha district.

headline: India simplifies visa regime, reduces categories to 9 from 13
brief:
India has rationalised its visa regime, reducing the number of main visa categories from 13 to nine and sub-categories from 49 to 23, in a move aimed at facilitating foreign tourist arrivals, medical travel and international student enrolment.
The Indian Ministry of Home...
body_html:
India has rationalised its visa regime, reducing the number of main visa categories from 13 to nine and sub-categories from 49 to 23, in a move aimed at facilitating foreign tourist arrivals, medical travel and international student enrolment.

The Indian Ministry of Home Affairs said the changes would make the visa framework more compact, coherent and responsive to the needs of foreign nationals visiting the country.

"Under Visa regime rationalization, main categories for Visa reduced from 13 to 09 and sub categories from 49 to 23," the ministry said on November 11.

The revised framework also reduces the number of fields applicants need to fill in visa application forms across all 23 sub-categories by 65 to 70 percent, making the application process easier and faster.

The changes are intended to minimise overlaps between visa categories and make it easier for visitors, patients, students, researchers, investors and business professionals to identify the appropriate visa for their travel purposes.

Under the revised medical visa framework, separate provisions have been retained for treatment under conventional and AYUSH systems.

The M-1 visa covers medical treatment other than that under AYUSH systems, while the M-3 visa is for treatment under AYUSH systems.

Both M-1 and M-3 visas, including their e-Visa variants, will generally be granted for one year with multiple entries.

Corresponding medical attendant visas have also been introduced, with M-2 visas available for attendants of M-1 visa holders and M-4 visas for attendants of M-3 visa holders.

The erstwhile Tourist Visa has been renamed the Visitor Visa to reflect a broader range of permitted activities beyond conventional tourism.

The new Visitor Visa category has been divided into two sub-categories, V-1 and V-2, allowing applicants to choose according to the nature and duration of their proposed visit.

Apart from tourism, the category covers short-term activities such as business meetings, medical consultations, wellness retreats, short-duration medical treatment and short courses in Indian languages, music, art and craft.

The Visitor Visa is granted for 30 days with multiple entries, according to the ministry.

Currently, India's e-Visa facility is processed through an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) system under 13 sub-categories and is available to nationals of 172 countries.

The ministry said the rationalisation was intended to promote legitimate travel, education, healthcare and economic engagement with India through clearer, purpose-based visa options.

The initiative was undertaken under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the guidance of Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation Amit Shah, it added.

headline: 137 fake Facebook accounts, pages using PM Tarique’s name, photos identified: State Minister
brief:
A total of 137 fake Facebook accounts, pages and groups using the name and photographs of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman have been identified by BanglaFact, State Minister for Information and Broadcasting Yasser Khan Choudhury told Parliament on Thursday.
This information...
body_html:
A total of 137 fake Facebook accounts, pages and groups using the name and photographs of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman have been identified by BanglaFact, State Minister for Information and Broadcasting Yasser Khan Choudhury told Parliament on Thursday.

This information was disclosed while replying to a starred question from BNP lawmaker Sherin Sultana (Women Seat-2) during the question-and-answer session in the House.

In absence of Information and Broadcasting Minister Andaleeve Rahman, the state minister on his behalf answered questions after the Parliament day’s proceedings began at 4:20pm with Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad, Bir Bikram.

Sherin Sultana wanted to know about the steps taken by the ministry to raise public awareness, ensure swift resolution of complaints and strengthen coordination among relevant agencies to prevent the circulation of manipulated images of women on social media, blackmail and defamation through fake accounts, and online harassment of children.

In his reply, Yasser Khan Choudhury said BanglaFact, the digital initiative of the Press Institute Bangladesh (PIB) under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, was actively working against fake information, disinformation, hate speech and attempts at character assassination circulated online.

He said BanglaFact has so far published 1,172 fact-checks, analyses, investigative reports, videos and reels to counter propaganda, malicious campaigns and misleading news.

Of these, 552 have been published since the present government assumed office.

The state minister said BanglaFact had earlier identified 19 websites that mimic newspapers and television channels to spread propaganda and disinformation.

He said BanglaFact has also identified more than 800 Facebook accounts and over 100 accounts on X spreading misleading and false information.

He said BanglaFact currently verified an average of three to five claims daily and publishes reports, reels and videos based on its findings.

A fact-checking manual will soon be published to facilitate the work of members of the public and journalists, he added.

body_html:
A listed ‘drug peddler’ was stabbed to death by miscreants at his residence in the Bakalia area of Chattogram city early Thursday.

The deceased was identified as Md Sobhan, 30, son of Nur Islam of Taktar Pool of Bakalia. He was wanted in a number of cases, including 18 drug-related ones, police said.

Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Bakalia Police Station Shahinur Alam said a group of miscreants stormed into Sobhan’s residence around 12:15am and stabbed him indiscriminately, leaving him injured.

Later, he was taken to Chattogram Medical College Hospital where doctors declared him dead.

The OC said they were working to find those involved in the killing.

Earlier, Sobhan had allegedly planned the murder of a man named Mohiuddin to maintain control and dominance over the drug trading in Taktar Pool area.

He was also accused of hiring hitmen and supplying them with foreign-made pistols and ammunition for the planned murder.

Locals suspected that long-standing disputes and rivalry over control of the area may have led to the killing.

However, the actual motive and identities of those involved will be determined through investigation, police said.

headline: Evil forces trying to create anarchy across country: Rizvi
brief:
BNP acting Secretary General and Prime Minister's Political Adviser Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Thursday alleged that evil forces were trying to resurface to undermine the country's democratic environment and create instability.
&l
body_html:
BNP acting Secretary General and Prime Minister's Political Adviser Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Thursday alleged that evil forces were trying to resurface to undermine the country's democratic environment and create instability.

“Attempts are being made to create anarchy across the country in a planned manner,” he said while addressing a discussion organised at North South University (NSU) marking National Revolution and Solidarity Day.

Rizvi said no initiative lacking public support could survive. “Although attempts are being made to carry out acts of sabotage in a planned manner, the people will resist them,” he said.

He alleged that attempts were being made to carry out anti-state activities with financial support from across the border. “Even the homes of women student leaders who played leading roles in recent movements have come under attack,” he said.

However, the BNP leader expressed confidence that such attempts to create artificial instability would not last long.

He called for building a sustainable and fear-free democratic environment to ensure that a culture of fear never returned to the country.

Rizvi also strongly criticised the education system and the role of the intellectual community during the previous regime.

Citing a report by Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB), he alleged that recruitment at all levels, from primary schools to public universities, had been influenced by financial transactions during the previous government.

The BNP leader also alleged that fabricated versions of history had been incorporated into textbooks, pushing the country's education system towards destruction.

Drawing examples from history, Rizvi said many renowned philosophers and writers in Germany had sided with fascism during Adolf Hitler's rule. “Similarly, many prominent intellectuals in Bangladesh worked in favour of the previous authoritarian government.”

Referring to the incident in which eminent writer and intellectual Badruddin Umar was not allowed to return to university teaching after independence, he said genuine education was not limited to earning certificates. “The true purpose of education lies in conscience, humanity and standing up for the truth during difficult times,” he said.

The discussion was chaired by North South University Vice-Chancellor Prof Abdul Hannan Chowdhury, while noted economist and National Professor Dr Mahbub Ullah spoke as the keynote discussant.

Members of the NSU Board of Trustees MA Kashem and Benajir Ahmed attended the programme as special guests.

NSU Pro-VC Prof Nasar U Ahmed delivered the welcome address.

brief:

Titled BTS: The Return, the fil
body_html:
A new Netflix documentary offers an intimate look at the global K-pop phenomenon BTS as the group reunites following nearly four years away from full-band activities.

Titled BTS: The Return, the film follows all seven members — RM, Jin, Jimin, V, Suga, Jung Kook and J-Hope — as they prepare for their comeback album ARIRANG, released Friday.

headline: Israel assassinates Al Jazeera reporter Anas al-Sharif in deadly Gaza strike as journalist casualties soar
brief: Israeli forces launched a deadly airstrike late Sunday in Gaza, killing prominent Al Jazeera correspondent Anas al-Sharif and several colleagues, sparking widespread condemnation and accusations of a deliberate campaign to silence journalists reporting the harsh realities...
body_html:
Israeli forces launched a deadly airstrike late Sunday in Gaza, killing prominent Al Jazeera correspondent Anas al-Sharif and several colleagues, sparking widespread condemnation and accusations of a deliberate campaign to silence journalists reporting the harsh realities of war.

The strike, confirmed by Israel and Gaza hospital officials, targeted a press site outside Gaza City’s main hospital, killing al-Sharif, fellow Al Jazeera reporter Mohamed Qreiqeh, four other journalists, and two civilians. Hospital authorities described the attack as a brutal blow to media freedom amid the ongoing conflict.

Israel’s military accused al-Sharif of leading a Hamas cell, claims dismissed by Al Jazeera and human rights advocates as baseless smears aimed at justifying the killings. This marks the first time in the 22-month war that Israel openly accepted responsibility for a journalist’s death, underscoring the deadly risk faced by reporters in the world’s deadliest conflict for the media.

Five Al Jazeera journalists killed in Gaza

Al Jazeera denounced the strike as a “targeted assassination” and accused Israeli officials of inciting violence against its team, who have been among the few voices delivering raw, frontline coverage of Gaza’s devastation, starvation, and relentless bombings.

The killing comes after months of escalating attacks on Al Jazeera journalists, including previous deaths and office raids, with the network banned in Israel and restricted in the occupied West Bank.

UN human rights experts and press freedom groups condemned the airstrike as a grave violation of international law, warning that Israel’s smear campaign is a calculated attempt to silence truth and evade accountability.

At funerals for al-Sharif, Qreiqeh, and their colleagues, hundreds, including journalists from across the globe, mourned the fallen and called for urgent international action to protect media workers in conflict zones.

Al-Sharif, known for his fearless reporting and emotional broadcasts highlighting Gaza’s humanitarian crisis, left a poignant farewell message expressing his unwavering commitment to truth before his death.

The Committee to Protect Journalists condemned the attack, urging the world to hold Israel accountable for targeting reporters, and highlighting that at least 186 journalists have been killed in Gaza during this conflict—making it the deadliest ever for the press.

Aamir Khan has come under fire online after his production house posted a tribute to the heroes of Operation Sindoor just hours before releasing the trailer for his upcoming film Sitaare Zameen Par on May 13.

The official X (formerly Twitter) account of Aamir Khan Productions shared a message saying, "Salute to the heroes of Operation Sindoor." The post sparked backlash, with many social media users accusing the actor of attempting to leverage a patriotic moment to draw attention to his film.

One user commented, "Kucha jada jaldi nahi kar di post?" (Haven't you posted too early?)—suggesting the timing was strategic rather than sincere.

Another post criticized several Bollywood stars by name, stating, "We as Indian should just ignore these morons @AKPPL_Official @iamsrk, @BeingSalmanKhan, @saifalikhan067. They earn their money here in India but at the time of adversity they want to show how intellectual they are. Probably they are also under the illusion about 72 virgins."

Yet another user speculated on the motives behind the message, writing, "Dekho koi movie ka announcement bhi ata hoga... Ye paise k liye bolte h lekin dil m Turkey and Pakistan h."

body_html:
President Joe Biden intends to bolster U.S. military support to Ukraine in the final months of his administration, U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken said on Wednesday, after Russia launched a sophisticated missile and drone attack on Kyiv.

The U.S. will “continue to shore up everything we’re doing for Ukraine to make sure that it can effectively defend itself against this Russian aggression,” Blinken told reporters at NATO headquarters, before planned meetings with allied envoys and Ukrainian officials.

Blinken warned that North Korea’s decision to send its troops into combat operations alongside Russian forces “demands and will get a firm response.” He didn't elaborate.

U.S., South Korean and Ukrainian intelligence assessments say up to 12,000 North Korean combat troops are being sent to the war. The bulk of those troops were expected to be deployed in Russia’s Kursk region where Ukrainian troops have seized a swathe of territory.

Russia’s early morning missile and drone attack was the first on Kyiv in 73 days. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said that Russia is intensifying its strikes, apparently in an effort to discourage Ukrainians from continuing the war, which is approaching its 1,000-day milestone.

Russia appears to be pressing its advantage as doubt swirls about how Washington might change policy on the war after Donald Trump takes office as U.S. president in January. The U.S. is the biggest provider of military help to Ukraine.

Trump has slammed the Biden administration for giving Kyiv tens of billions of dollars in aid and has promised to quickly end the conflict. Ukraine’s international backers fear that any rushed settlement would mostly benefit Russian President Vladimir Putin.

body_html:
Debutant fast bowler Saqib Khan spearheaded Pakistan's fightback in the first cricket Test with a seven-wicket haul, as Sri Lanka were dismissed for a 12-run first-innings lead on Thursday.

Saqib claimed 7-130, making the most of ideal overcast conditions with his sharp swing bowling to bowl out Sri Lanka for 446 within the first 90 minutes of Day 4. The visitors lost their final six wickets for just 42 runs.

Saqib dismissed Asitha Fernando through a review, with the batter caught behind to give wicketkeeper Ghazi Ghori his sixth catch of the innings. The 31-year-old became only the fourth Pakistan bowler, after Mohammad Nazir, Mohammad Zahid and Abrar Ahmed, to take seven wickets in an innings on his Test debut.

Fernando had earlier trapped Tayyab Arif, one of Pakistan's four debutants, leg before wicket. Pakistan reached 39-1 in their second innings at lunch, taking their overall lead to 27 runs. Azan Awais was unbeaten on 16, while Mohammad Taha was not out on 12.

The greenish pitch, which had produced only one wicket on the second day, came alive under favourable bowling conditions, with seven wickets falling in the first session on Thursday.

Saqib delivered a relentless eight-over spell on the fourth morning, taking five wickets for 25 runs after Sri Lanka resumed at a commanding 404-4, built around centuries from Dhananjaya de Silva and captain Kusal Mendis.

He struck with the fifth ball of the morning to break the 249-run partnership, finding the outside edge of de Silva's bat. The batter, who had been unbeaten on 167 overnight, could add nothing to his score.

Saud Shakeel, who dropped de Silva on 38 on the third day, missed another opportunity when he spilled a low catch offered by Mendis. But two balls later, Ghori took another outstanding diving catch off Saqib's probing delivery outside the off stump to end the Sri Lankan captain's innings at 119.

Sonal Dinusha, one of Sri Lanka's rising talents who had scored three centuries and two half-centuries in his previous five Tests, made 20 before attempting an expansive drive against Saqib and edging the ball to the slip cordon. The wicket completed the fast bowler's five-wicket haul.

Milan Rathnayake took Sri Lanka past Pakistan's first-innings total of 434-9 declared with a pull shot for four off Razaullah. Saqib then claimed two more wickets, while Razaullah (1-140) completed Pakistan's impressive morning by having Rathnayake caught at deep fine leg.
