headline: FIFA says bids for 2031, 2035 Women's World Cups meet hosting requirements
brief:
FIFA has released its evaluation reports on the joint bids to host the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cups, confirming that both proposals have met the minimum hosting requirements and will be submitted to member associations for a vote later this month.
The United States, ...
body_html:
FIFA has released its evaluation reports on the joint bids to host the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cups, confirming that both proposals have met the minimum hosting requirements and will be submitted to member associations for a vote later this month.

The United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica have jointly submitted the sole bid for the 2031 tournament, which will see the competition expanded from 32 to 48 teams. The 2035 edition has a joint bid from England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

The evaluation reports, published by FIFA on Wednesday, found both bids compliant with the minimum requirements ahead of the vote at the Extraordinary FIFA Congress on November 23.

According to FIFA, the 2031 bid benefits from a strong foundation, particularly following the United States' experience of co-hosting the men's World Cup with Mexico and Canada, as well as staging the 2025 Club World Cup. The women's tournament is projected to attract 4.5 million spectators.

The 2031 proposal features 20 potential stadiums across the four countries, including 14 in the United States, four in Mexico, and one each in Jamaica and Costa Rica. Most of the proposed venues are existing facilities, while the new RFK Stadium in Washington, D.C., has yet to be constructed.

Four stadiums have been shortlisted as potential venues for the final: Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, AT&T Stadium near Dallas, SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles and MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey.

Seven proposed venues in the United States and one in Mexico currently have artificial playing surfaces and would need to install natural grass for the tournament. During this summer's men's World Cup, several venues, including Lumen Field in Seattle, used temporary natural-grass pitches.

FIFA also noted that US government agencies had submitted letters of support, committing to meeting requirements related to immigration, visas, work permits and security.

"Accordingly, while certain commitments require further engagement, there is a sound basis for confidence that continued dialogue and collaboration with the relevant government agencies should support the successful organization and delivery of the tournament, should the bid be successful," FIFA said.

The four nations behind the 2035 bid have adopted the theme "All Together", highlighting their joint commitment and experience in hosting major international sporting events.

"The bid draws on the shared commitment of the four member associations and their experience (both current and upcoming) in hosting major international sporting events, including the UEFA Women's Euro 2022 and the UEFA Euro 2028."

The 2035 proposal includes 15 host cities and 19 stadiums across the four nations, with 14 venues in England, two in Northern Ireland, one in Scotland and two in Wales. London's Wembley Stadium has been proposed as the venue for the final.

Meanwhile, FIFA on Wednesday announced the draw procedure for next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil. The draw will take place in Rio de Janeiro on December 11.

The 32 participating teams will be divided into four pots of eight. The four highest-ranked teams will be kept apart until the later stages of the competition, provided they finish at the top of their respective groups.

The seeding will be based on FIFA's rankings to be published on December 7. In the current standings, defending champions Spain are ranked first, followed by the United States, Germany and England.

body_html:
Bangladesh stormed into the semi-finals of the SAFF Championship as Group A champions after thrashing Sri Lanka 4-0 in their final group-stage match at the National Stadium in Dhaka on Wednesday night.

Captain Hamza Choudhury marked his SAFF Championship debut with a goal as Bangladesh produced an impressive performance in front of the home crowd.

Shamit Shome opened the scoring in the eighth minute before Hamza doubled the lead with a superb individual effort in the 44th minute.

Farhaan Ali Wahid extended Bangladesh's lead in the 53rd minute with a brilliant solo effort, while Rakib Hossain completed the rout in the 87th minute.

body_html:
The third one-day international between India and New Zealand was abandoned without a ball being bowled on Tuesday due to persistent rain.

India won the toss after a delay of more than two hours caused by a wet outfield and intermittent showers, but conditions never improved enough for play to begin.

Officials called off the match shortly before 7pm local time as heavier, more persistent rain made it impossible to prepare Seddon Park before the 8pm cut-off time.

Rain had also disrupted the first two matches of the series. India won the opening ODI in Auckland by five wickets and the second in Wellington by four runs, with both matches decided under the Duckworth-Lewis system.

The teams will now travel to Mount Maunganui on New Zealand's North Island for the fourth and fifth ODIs, scheduled for Friday and Sunday.

India have secured at least a series victory, while New Zealand can still draw the series level.

headline: CF Montreal put up for sale, club's future in city uncertain
brief:
The Saputo family has initiated the process of selling CF Montreal, putting the Major League Soccer club's future in the Canadian city in question.
The club announced the decision
body_html:
The Saputo family has initiated the process of selling CF Montreal, putting the Major League Soccer club's future in the Canadian city in question.

The club announced the decision on Monday, saying the family, which has owned the team for more than three decades, was beginning the process of finding new ownership.

The family has been associated with the club since 1992, when it was known as the Montreal Impact and competed in the American Professional Soccer League. The team joined MLS in 2012.

“After more than three decades of commitment, we believe this is the appropriate time to begin the process of identifying new ownership for CF Montreal,” Joey Saputo said in a statement.

He described the club as a central part of the family's lives, saying they had invested considerable time, effort and resources in building it.

Saputo also thanked the fans, saying their passion and loyalty had been central to the club.

The family would prefer to sell the team to a buyer willing to keep it in Montreal, Saputo said, although he did not rule out the possibility of the club moving to another city under new ownership.

The announcement comes after CF Montreal endured its worst season in MLS, finishing at the bottom of the Eastern Conference with a record of six wins, 20 losses and eight draws.

Speaking at a news conference on Monday, Saputo, however, insisted that the decision to sell was not driven by the team's on-field performance or financial concerns.

headline: Meghan makes first public appearance since father's arrest as Harry calls for tech transparency
brief:
Prince Harry called on technology companies to be more transparent about issues affecting children as he and his wife Meghan made their first public appearance on Tuesday since her father was arrested on suspicion of possessing child sexual abuse material.
Harry delivere...
body_html:
Prince Harry called on technology companies to be more transparent about issues affecting children as he and his wife Meghan made their first public appearance on Tuesday since her father was arrested on suspicion of possessing child sexual abuse material.

Harry delivered the remarks at the European Parliament in Brussels during the inauguration of a memorial honouring children who died after suffering harm linked to social media. The installation, called the Lost Screen Memorial, features replicas of oversized smartphones, each displaying a photograph of a deceased child on its home screen.

Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex and formerly known as Meghan Markle, was initially scheduled to speak alongside Harry but later withdrew because she was not emotionally strong enough, according to a person familiar with her decision. However, she accompanied her husband to the event.

The allegations against her father, Thomas Markle Sr., emerged last month. He was ordered to jail on Tuesday after removing an electronic monitoring device from his ankle, days after being charged with possessing child sexual abuse material.

Appearing emotional during his speech, Harry urged social media companies not to expose children to content that they would not want their own children to see.

He also called for greater transparency and cooperation from technology firms, particularly in helping parents access their children's devices and social media accounts to understand what they experienced online.

"For many parents, even though their child killed themselves, they've had to wait years – in some instances, eight years – to get access to their child's phone," Harry said.

He added that some parents had been prevented from discovering the circumstances of their children's deaths because of companies' privacy policies, saying such restrictions were unacceptable.

"That cannot be right," he said.

headline: Appeals court orders narrower LinkedIn disclosure of journalists’ communications in leak probe
brief:
A US federal appeals court ruled Tuesday that a judge must narrow an order directing LinkedIn to hand over journalists’ communications to the Trump administration as part of an investigation into the leaking of classified information.
A three-judge panel of the 4th
body_html:
A US federal appeals court ruled Tuesday that a judge must narrow an order directing LinkedIn to hand over journalists’ communications to the Trump administration as part of an investigation into the leaking of classified information.

A three-judge panel of the 4th US Circuit Court of Appeals said the government cannot demand a blanket disclosure of a wide range of user records belonging to the journalists, whose employer was not identified in court documents.

Allowing the government to collect reporters’ records wholesale to identify their confidential sources would undermine informed public discourse and harm democratic health, Judge J. Harvie Wilkinson III wrote in the unanimous ruling.

However, the panel rejected LinkedIn’s request to completely overturn the district court’s disclosure order, describing it as substantially overbroad. It said the journalists’ First Amendment rights must be weighed against the administration’s responsibility to safeguard national security information.

"Serious security and speech claims are in tension in this case. There is space under law for both," Wilkinson wrote. He was nominated to the appeals court by former Republican President Ronald Reagan.

The panel also included Judge James Andrew Wynn, nominated by Democratic President Barack Obama, and Judge Nicole G. Berner, nominated by Democratic President Joe Biden.

The disclosure order was issued by US District Judge Elizabeth Hanes, a Biden nominee based in Newport News, Virginia, and was subsequently challenged by LinkedIn.

The Trump administration launched the leak investigation after an unidentified news organisation published a report detailing a top-secret US military operation in a foreign country, disclosing classified information.

During the 18-month period covered by the court order, the journalists under investigation had reported nearly 1,000 stories on a wide range of subjects.

The order would have exposed every confidential source with whom the targeted journalists communicated through LinkedIn during that period.

Although such a disclosure could help the government identify sources relevant to its investigation, it would also inevitably expose numerous other confidential sources unrelated to the probe, Wilkinson wrote.

The appeals court sent the case back to Hanes, instructing her to revise and narrow the disclosure order.

The district court was justified in giving the government considerable leeway to pursue its investigation and protect its integrity, Wilkinson said. However, he stressed that such authority has limits and that courts should not approve disclosure requests simply because the requested records can be collected easily.

headline: Asif urges youth to use AI for tackling social challenges
brief: Prime Minister's Adviser on Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Rehan Asif Asad has called on young people to step forward and use artificial intelligence (AI) to address various social challenges.
body_html:
Prime Minister's Adviser on Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Rehan Asif Asad has called on young people to step forward and use artificial intelligence (AI) to address various social challenges.

"Learning and adopting new technologies alone will not be enough to harness the potential of AI. We must also know how to apply these technologies to solve real-life problems," Asif said while addressing the closing ceremony of the second edition of "FutureMakers," an AI-based innovation competition organised by Grameenphone at a city hotel on Tuesday.

He said AI is transforming industries and economies worldwide, and it is crucial to ensure that young people have the necessary tools, skills and opportunities to keep pace with this change.

Asif stressed that, for Bangladesh to fully tap into the potential of AI, young people should be encouraged not only to learn new technologies but also to apply them to real-life challenges.

He said initiatives like FutureMakers create opportunities for students to work with AI, build their skills and turn innovative ideas into effective solutions.

The adviser expressed hope that such initiatives could play an important role in building a skilled workforce for the future and in the growth of the country's digital economy.

Team Labdhab emerged champion in the competition with "EcoClip," a device that can be attached to a regular stethoscope to detect possible early signs of heart disease.

Team River Sentinel became the first runner-up for developing an AI-based system to forecast river erosion. The project can identify vulnerable areas and issue early warnings.

Team Zinxed finished third with "Spasto AI," an AI-powered speech therapy app for people with speech difficulties. The app allows users to practise at home and track their progress.

The three winning teams received prize money of Tk 3 lakh, Tk 2 lakh and Tk 1 lakh, respectively. Members of the winning teams will also get the opportunity to join Grameenphone's "Next Business Leader" and "Nextern Internship" programmes directly.

headline: Australia to establish AI safety regulator after OpenAI agent breaches government website
brief:
Australia plans to establish an artificial intelligence safety regulator following a breach of a government health department website by an unauthorised OpenAI agent in June, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday.
The proposed regulator will enf
body_html:
Australia plans to establish an artificial intelligence safety regulator following a breach of a government health department website by an unauthorised OpenAI agent in June, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said Tuesday.

The proposed regulator will enforce legally mandated AI safety standards, described as among the world's most advanced, on all leading AI companies seeking to operate in Australia, Albanese said.

Companies violating the standards will face financial penalties, although the government has yet to specify the amount.

“When it comes to the generational opportunity that artificial intelligence offers Australia, I've been very clear: our task is to make sure we shape AI rather than AI shape us,” Albanese told reporters.

He said Australia wanted to take a leading role in the sector while ensuring that the country benefited from AI's potential.

Under the proposed standards, AI companies will be required to maintain security measures throughout the development and deployment of their models and identify and manage serious risks.

They will also have to promptly notify the government of incidents involving “misaligned behaviour” that goes against developers' intended instructions.

Australian government documents define frontier AI as the most sophisticated models operating at the cutting edge of existing technological capabilities.

Albanese previously told OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman that the US-based company had taken too long to inform the Australian government about the breach, which occurred three months before the company reported it in September.

The incident marked the first known case of such a breach involving the technology.

On June 18, information was accessed without authorisation from the public-facing Medicare Statistics Reporting Service portal and was subsequently made public. However, it remains unclear whether the incident violated any Australian laws.

OpenAI apologised in September for both the breach and its delayed response.

“We are sorry and working to do better in the future,” the company said in a statement, acknowledging that it should also have handled its response more effectively.

A government inquiry into the incident made several recommendations, including that authorities consider changes to existing laws.

Albanese said his government had accepted all the inquiry's recommendations, including those concerning possible criminal law reforms.

“The point is law needs to get ahead of and in some cases make sure that it catches up with what is a very fast-changing world. And to be clear, Australia is a first-mover in these areas,” he said.

The proposed AI regulator would follow Australia's establishment of an eSafety Commissioner in 2015, an office that describes itself as the world's first government agency dedicated to online safety.

Since December last year, the commissioner has been enforcing a world-first ban preventing Australian children under 16 from holding accounts on popular social media platforms.

headline: Meloni blames pro-Russian hackers for leak of Italian foreign minister's data
brief:
Italian Foreign Minister and Vice Premier Antonio Tajani said Saturday that his personal data has been leaked on the dark web, exposing him and his family to ongoing threats and intimidation by cybercriminals seeking to buy further confidential details.
In
body_html:
Italian Foreign Minister and Vice Premier Antonio Tajani said Saturday that his personal data has been leaked on the dark web, exposing him and his family to ongoing threats and intimidation by cybercriminals seeking to buy further confidential details.

In a separate statement, Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers for the leak, expressing solidarity with Tajani and calling attempts to sell confidential information about government officials a matter of grave concern that must be addressed with utmost determination.

Tajani made the announcement on social media following a string of recent European security incidents, including flight-diverting hoax bomb threats, threats against broadcasters, attacks on supermarket refrigeration systems, and drone incursions.

While Tajani did not specify the nature of the leaked data or directly name responsible parties, he suggested the cyberthreat is ongoing, reiterated Italy's support for Ukraine, and vowed not to be intimidated.

"I will not allow myself to be intimidated in any way," Tajani said, pledging to strengthen international cooperation to defend his ministry and Italy.

headline: Rashed Khan brands Jamaat ameer as ‘national liar’ over party's meeting with Indian intelligence
brief:
Prime Minister’s Political Assistant Rashed Khan on Wednesday called Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman a “national liar” over the controversy surrounding a meeting between Jamaat leaders and an Indian intelligence official.
In
body_html:
Prime Minister’s Political Assistant Rashed Khan on Wednesday called Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman a “national liar” over the controversy surrounding a meeting between Jamaat leaders and an Indian intelligence official.

In a post on his verified Facebook account, Rashed said Shafiqur had earned the reputation of a national liar before the entire nation.

Responding to a remark by Shafiqur in the parliament, he said, “Rashed Khan plays with information, not falsehoods,”.

Rashed then said, “Mr Shafiqur Rahman, you have earned the reputation of a national liar before the entire nation. If you have any sense of shame, do not enter the Jatiya Sangsad again. Even if you do, apologise for your statement today.”

“Do we need any further evidence of the meeting between Jamaat Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar and an Indian intelligence official?” Rashed asked in the post.

It may be mentioned Rashed has been publicly stating a meeting took place recently between visiting officers of Indian intelligence and Jamaat e Islami's senior leadership. He has even published a video purporting to be footage of the meeting.

Rashed said all the country's prominent journalists had information about the meeting.

Rashed further said the Jamaat ameer had ended his own and his party's political credibility by making false statements in the presence of 350 members of parliament in the Jatiya Sangsad.

Leader of the Opposition Dr Shafiqur Rahman on Wednesday challenged Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed to clarify which political party he was referring to when he suggested that a party had links to foreign intelligence agencies allegedly encouraging unrest in Bangladesh.

Speaking in Parliament following the minister’s statement under Rule 300, he said Salahuddin had made some indirect remarks, including an allegation that instigations were coming from across the border.

“I agree with him on that. However, there are allegations that a political party has an understanding with a foreign intelligence agency. Is there any connection between that party and the instigations? Which party is he referring to? I urge him to clarify,” said Shafiqur, also the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami ameer.

The opposition leader also rejected any suggestion that Jamaat had met representatives of foreign intelligence agencies, saying the party had no history of holding meetings with any country's intelligence agency.

“We are a political party. We meet our political opponents and friends, if there are any. Why would we meet an intelligence agency?” he said.

These are the remarks Rashed targeted in his post.

headline: India won't get int’l support if it interferes in Bangladesh over Hasina: Rizvi
brief: BNP acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Wednesday said India would receive no international support if it interfered in Bangladesh's internal affairs over ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who had been convicted of crimes against humanity.
body_html:
BNP acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Wednesday said India would receive no international support if it interfered in Bangladesh's internal affairs over ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who had been convicted of crimes against humanity.

“Hasina did not find refuge in other countries but was given shelter by a particular country. If that country directly or indirectly interferes in Bangladesh's internal affairs through various incidents, it will not receive international support,” he said.

Rizvi also said the people of Bangladesh would also resist any such interference and thwart conspiracies.

He made the remarks while speaking to journalists at the BNP's Nayapaltan central office in the afternoon.

Commenting on the recent activities of Awami League, whose activities are banned, the BNP leader said it was following an old tactic of exploiting a chaotic situation for political gains. “They are trying to instil fear and panic among people through terrorism and anarchy to reap political benefits. I think they are living in a fool's paradise,” he said.

He said the constitutional guarantee of access to legal remedies was a fundamental right of citizens, but argued that those who had committed crimes against humanity could not claim such rights in the same manner.

Rizvi alleged that bloodshed and killings had been central to the AL's political agenda and culture, and that the party was now trying to return through the same approach.

He, however, said peace-loving people committed to democracy would not allow it.

On the law-and-order situation, the BNP leader said it was gradually improving, although some setbacks had occurred.

He alleged that associates of the ousted regime were deliberately trying to undermine law and order through bomb attacks and arson attacks on buses and vehicles.

Rizvi argued that there was no deterioration in the country's social order. “Rather, a defeated political force is deliberately trying to create an artificial impression of insecurity and social disorder.”

He also criticised what he described as the renewed assertiveness of some people associated with the previous regime.

The BNP leader said they were now speaking loudly on television talk shows despite remaining silent when innocent children, teenagers and students of universities, colleges and schools were being killed indiscriminately.

He said the government should look into such matters. “We believe in freedom of expression for everyone. But can robbers and terrorists also claim freedom of expression?” he asked.

headline: BNP leaders must work as Tarique Rahman's ambassadors: Zabihullah
brief: Prime Minister's Adviser for Public Administration and BNP standing committee member Md Ismail Zabihullah on Wednesday said BNP leaders and activists must work as ambassadors of party Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman instead of relying solely on his image and po...
body_html:
Prime Minister's Adviser for Public Administration and BNP standing committee member Md Ismail Zabihullah on Wednesday said BNP leaders and activists must work as ambassadors of party Chairman and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman instead of relying solely on his image and popularity.

“We cannot just sit back relying on Tarique Rahman's image. Each of us must work as his ambassador and strengthen his hands,” he said.

He made these remarks at a discussion session arranged by Jatiotabadi Tati Dal at the jatiya press club in the city, to mark the November 7 National Revolution and Solidarity Day.

The BNP leader said party leaders and activists must understand the country's history and make others aware of it to succeed in the contemporary political struggle.

He also called for unity across political, religious, and social differences to protect the country's independence, sovereignty, and territorial integrity.

“Democracy allows different parties, opinions, and paths. But whenever the questions of national sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity arise, we must stand united, regardless of religion, political affiliation, or whether we live in the plains or hills,” he said.

Referring to the country's political challenges, he said the lessons of November 7 should inspire people to remain united and prevent the return of fascism.

He also highlighted the contributions of former President Ziaur Rahman to the country's economic development, particularly in agriculture, the garment industry, overseas employment, and the growth of private entrepreneurship.

He said Ziaur Rahman had taken initiatives to revive the rural economy through canal excavation, promote agricultural production, and encourage private-sector investment.

The BNP leader expressed hope that the government led by Tarique Rahman would continue Zia's initiatives and work to develop the handloom sector and rural industries.

He said the goal should be to build a state where workers receive their fair rights, young people find employment, and Bangladesh can stand with dignity in the international arena.

“Chhatra League and Awami Lea
body_html:
Prime Minister's Political Assistant Rashed Khan on Wednesday alleged that Awami League and Chhatra League activists were now trying to survive by operating covertly within Jamaat-e-Islami.

“Chhatra League and Awami League activists are now trying to survive by going undercover within Jamaat. Jamaat-Shibir, meanwhile, is giving Awami League miscreants space in their ranks to increase their numbers,” he said.

Rashed made the remarks in a post on his verified Facebook account.

He accused Jamaat-e-Islami and its student wing Islami Chhatra Shibir of subtly normalising the alleged terrorist activities of the banned Awami League instead of taking a strong stand against its activists.

Rashed questioned whether Sheikh Hasina or her then home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal knew that Shadik Kayem, while serving as president of Shibir's Dhaka University unit, maintained covert links with the Chhatra League.

He also asked whether the AL government had intelligence about Jamaat-Shibir members across the country who, according to him, secretly participated in Chhatra League and Awami League politics.

Rashed further alleged that Jamaat-Shibir had taught the AL the tactics of covert politics.

He questioned why Jamaat-Shibir had not taken a stronger role in resisting AL activities and arson attacks, suggesting that the party might have two reasons for not taking to the streets forcefully at this moment.

First, he said, Jamaat-Shibir might believe that unrest created by the AL would weaken the BNP government.

If the government became weak, the party could gain importance as the opposition, as the government might then seek its assistance in tackling the AL.

Jamaat-Shibir could use such cooperation as a bargaining tool to secure influence over government affairs while remaining in opposition, he said.

As a second possible reason, Rashed referred to a recent meeting between a Jamaat delegation, including Mia Golam Parwar and ATM Masum, and intelligence officials of an unnamed country.

He said Jamaat had denied holding the meeting, but argued that the denial had put the party in a difficult position.

Rashed speculated that the discussion might have involved a suggestion that Jamaat, as the opposition in parliament, should focus on its own bid for power rather than constantly opposing the AL. He suggested the party might have been advised to let the AL carry out its activities while Jamaat pursued its political ambitions.

However, regardless of which of the two explanations was correct, Rashed said, Jamaat-Shibir would not succeed in achieving its objectives.

He called for collective resistance against what he described as an AL-Jamaat conspiracy to weaken the BNP government for political gain.

headline: Fascism could raise its head again if justice for July victims remains unfinished: Deputy Speaker
brief: Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal on Wednesday warned that fascism could return if justice for the July victims remained unfinished, expressing concern over what he described as attempts by fascist forces to stage a comeback before the wounds of the uprising had heale...
body_html:
Deputy Speaker Barrister Kayser Kamal on Wednesday warned that fascism could return if justice for the July victims remained unfinished, expressing concern over what he described as attempts by fascist forces to stage a comeback before the wounds of the uprising had healed.

“I am expressing my highest level of dismay. The bloodstains have yet to dry. Only in July-August, 1,400 mothers lost their children. Their cries have not yet faded. The trial has not been completed, yet the fascists are sending signals. We should be ashamed,” he added.

He was speaking at a mock parliament titled 'Youth Manifesto', organised by IID at Bangla Academy in the capital.

Calling on young people to take a more active role in shaping the country, Kayser Kamal said they are the ones capable of bringing about meaningful change.

“I would urge you: let us start a new era in our country. If we cannot make a meaningful impact, fascism may return. Look, it is already peeping from India,” he said.

Questioning why young people are now staying at home, he recalled that they had taken to the streets voluntarily during the anti-fascist movement, without responding to the call of any particular political party.

They had faced bullets to protect the motherland, restore democracy, establish voting rights and the rule of law, and secure constitutional rights, he said.

“It is unfortunate if you now fold your hands and retreat into your homes. We have to be united,” he said.

He alleged that acts of terrorism are taking place in Bangladesh at the direction of forces from a neighbouring country, while the bloodstains on streets in Dhaka and elsewhere had yet to dry and the tears of the 1,400 bereaved mothers had not ceased.

The deputy speaker urged young people to ensure meaningful participation in rebuilding society and establishing a democratic political culture.

He said the country's politics would not be free from criminalisation unless educated, compassionate people committed to public service and social welfare became actively involved.

Expressing concern over divisions that had emerged after what he called the country's “second independence”, Kayser Kamal said constructive criticism was necessary, but all should work together in the interests of democracy and the country.

“Unfortunately, the unity that was forged during the 2024 student-people's uprising is not being maintained, or at least it does not appear to be maintained,” he said, urging young people to create a meaningful impact and help take the country towards democratic governance.

He also criticised what he described as self-centred tendencies among some politicians, saying many worked to establish their own parties, personal stature or families rather than prioritising the country.

headline: Shadik Kayem might be involved in crude bomb blasts at DU: JCD leader Nasir
brief: Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) General Secretary Nasir Uddin Nasir on Tuesday alleged that Dhaka University Central Students' Union (DUCSU) Vice-President Shadik Kayem might have been involved in crude bomb explosions on the university campus.
body_html:
Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) General Secretary Nasir Uddin Nasir on Tuesday alleged that Dhaka University Central Students' Union (DUCSU) Vice-President Shadik Kayem might have been involved in crude bomb explosions on the university campus.

"We believe he [Shadik Kayem] might have links to the crude bomb explosions. In 2014-15, Shadik Kayem was seen in Chhatra League processions aimed at suppressing the movements of the BNP and Chhatra Dal. He has an old connection. To preserve that connection, he is not standing beside the students," Nasir said.

He made the remarks while speaking to reporters in front of the Teacher-Student Centre (TSC) at Dhaka University in the afternoon.

Referring to what he described as Shadik Kayem's direct links with the banned Bangladesh Chhatra League in the past, Nasir alleged that Chhatra Shibir had previously supported the activities of the Chhatra League through covert politics and that its leaders and activists were still supporting its violent activities.

He also criticised the DUCSU leader for spending time with his family in response to an invitation from what he called terrorist leader Saddam (BCL president Saddam Hossain), describing it as shameful, saying students would not accept such a position after the mass uprising.

"We believe that while the country is moving forward following the verdict delivered by the people in February, Shadik Kayem and others are making misleading statements. Taking advantage of this, Chhatra League is exploding crude bombs," the JCD leader said.

Alleging that Shadik Kayem had been elected illegally, he questioned whether the DUCSU vice-president had fulfilled even his minimum responsibilities over the crude bomb explosions on the campus in recent days.

Meanwhile, in a post on his verified Facebook account in the evening, Nasir alleged that Chhatra Shibir had remained silent during the July uprising so that none of its leaders would be harmed if the Chhatra League remained in power.

"Even now, they are maintaining the same silence so that they are not harmed if the Chhatra League returns. They will approach the Chhatra League and say that they did not obstruct its return in any way. Then they will remain safe under its shadow," he wrote.

headline: Dutch govt launches programmes to boost Bangladeshi SMEs' export readiness
brief: The Netherlands-based Centre for the Promotion of Imports from developing countries (CBI) has launched two programmes to improve environmental sustainability, social compliance and export readiness among Bangladesh's small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the home textile...
body_html:
The Netherlands-based Centre for the Promotion of Imports from developing countries (CBI) has launched two programmes to improve environmental sustainability, social compliance and export readiness among Bangladesh's small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the home textiles and leather sectors.

The programmes, titled “Sustainable Home Textiles Bangladesh (2025–2030)” and “Bangladesh Leather x Decent Work (2025–2029),” were launched at the Bangladesh-Netherlands Sustainable Trade Forum 2026 in Dhaka on Wednesday.

The forum was organised by CBI, part of the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), under the commission of the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Commerce, Industries, Textiles and Jute Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir said the Netherlands could help cottage, micro, small and medium enterprises access the European market and explore new export opportunities.

Dutch Ambassador to Bangladesh Joris van Bommel described compliance requirements as an opportunity for businesses to improve standards and enter higher-value markets.

CBI Managing Director Judith Arends said the programmes would focus on workplace health and fire safety, fair working conditions, gender inclusiveness and workers' representation.

The home textiles programme will promote sustainable production through water management, natural dyeing and alternative materials, including three pilot initiatives on natural dyes, wastewater treatment and financing.

The leather programme will support small leather goods producers in improving workplace conditions and meeting European market requirements.

Bangladesh has around 11.7 million economic units employing 30.6 million people, while SMEs contribute an estimated 25 percent to GDP.

Around 170 representatives from government, businesses, financial institutions and development organisations attended the forum.

headline: Bangladesh's RMG exports to EU grow 2.79% in July-Oct
brief: Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) exports to the European Union (EU) reached US$6.43 billion during the July–October period of the fiscal year FY2026–27, marking a 2.79 percent increase from $6.26 billion recorded a year earlier, according to Export Promotion Bureau (...
body_html:
Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) exports to the European Union (EU) reached US$6.43 billion during the July–October period of the fiscal year FY2026–27, marking a 2.79 percent increase from $6.26 billion recorded a year earlier, according to Export Promotion Bureau (EPB) data compiled by Bangladesh Apparel Voice (BAV).

However, the growth remained heavily concentrated, with Spain single-handedly carrying nearly all of the expansion. Exports to Spain surged 13.36 percent to reach $1.448 billion—an increase of $170.6 million—which accounts for about 98 percent of the EU’s total gain of $174.5 million. With this stellar performance, Spain now commands 22.51 percent of Bangladesh’s total EU apparel exports, overtaking Germany.

Germany, previously the leading single market, completely stalled during the four-month period, inching up a negligible 0.01 percent to $1.439 billion and holding a 22.37 percent market share.

Among other European destinations, the Netherlands registered an 8.68 percent growth to $784.6 million, and Poland grew 2.85 percent to $545.9 million. In contrast, exports to France dropped by 7.87 percent to $611.1 million, while shipments to all other EU countries combined fell 1.34 percent to $1.60 billion. Collectively, the top five markets accounted for 75.1 percent of Bangladesh's total EU apparel exports during the July–October timeframe.

In October alone, RMG exports to the EU rose by a modest 1.10 percent to $1.53 billion. Germany remained the largest single market for the month at $315.7 million (+0.59%), closely followed by Spain at $299.2 million (+11.95%). Meanwhile, the Netherlands grew 7.62 percent to $187.1 million. Conversely, France suffered a sharp contraction, plunging 15.22 percent to $161.7 million, and Poland declined 4.49 percent to $144.0 million.

Market analysts point out that EU growth is currently exceptionally narrow. Excluding Spain's robust performance, Bangladesh’s overall apparel exports to the European Union would have remained virtually flat over the four-month period, weighed down by Germany's stagnation and France's ongoing decline.

headline: Bangladesh, Kuwait see strong potential for joint investment in multiple sectors
brief: Business leaders and entrepreneurs from Bangladesh and Kuwait have identified significant potential for joint investment in several sectors, including plastics, ceramics and leather goods, expressing their interest in strengthening bilateral trade, investment and economic...
body_html:
Business leaders and entrepreneurs from Bangladesh and Kuwait have identified significant potential for joint investment in several sectors, including plastics, ceramics and leather goods, expressing their interest in strengthening bilateral trade, investment and economic cooperation between the two countries.

The prospects were discussed at a virtual meeting between a Bangladeshi business delegation and the Kuwait Chamber of Commerce and Industry, organised by the Federation of Bangladesh Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FBCCI) on Wednesday.

The meeting was chaired by FBCCI Administrator Md Fazlul Hoque and attended by representatives of the Kuwait Chamber, FBCCI officials, diplomats and leading industrial entrepreneurs from Bangladesh.

Fazlul highlighted the longstanding friendly relations between the two countries and invited Kuwaiti entrepreneurs to invest in Bangladesh.

Highlighting Bangladesh's strong capabilities in leather, plastics, ceramics, processed food, readymade garments and ICT, he stressed the need for joint ventures to capitalise on emerging economic opportunities.

Bangladesh's Counsellor (Political and AIOC) in Kuwait, Mohammad Moniruzzaman, said Bangladesh has significant export potential in Kuwait, particularly in readymade garments, leather and leather goods, ICT and plastics, given the country's strong purchasing power and market opportunities.

He said the Bangladesh Embassy in Kuwait was working actively to strengthen communication and partnerships between businesspeople and investors from the two countries.

During the open discussion, Bangladesh Plastic Goods Manufacturers and Exporters Association President Md Shamim Ahmed invited Kuwaiti entrepreneurs to invest in Bangladesh's petrochemical industry.

Ahsan Khan Chowdhury, chairman and chief executive officer of PRAN-RFL Group, said Bangladesh imports a substantial volume of petrochemical and petroleum products from Kuwait, creating significant opportunities for joint investment in the sector.

He also called for resolving visa-related complications to facilitate business activities and movement between the two countries.

Bangladesh Ceramic Manufacturers and Exporters Association President Mainul Islam invited Kuwaiti investors to explore opportunities in Bangladesh's ceramics sector.

Considering the country's existing constraints in electricity and gas supplies, he also highlighted the potential for joint ventures to establish tableware ceramic factories in Kuwait.

In response, Abdul Aziz, a representative of the Kuwait Chamber, highlighted the export potential of Bangladeshi ceramic finishing products for Kuwait's housing and construction industry.

Kuwait Chamber of Commerce and Industry Deputy Director General Imad Al-Zayed assured that the organisation would play an active role in facilitating information exchange and strengthening business connections between entrepreneurs from Bangladesh and Kuwait.

FBCCI Secretary General Md Alamgir, business leaders and representatives of the Bangladesh Embassy in Kuwait also joined the virtual meeting.

headline: Dollar crosses Tk 125 in banking channels amid soaring fuel import costs
brief:
The exchange rate of the US dollar in Bangladesh’s banking channels has crossed Tk 125, driven by a surge in demand for fuel and petroleum imports, defying various stabilization measures by Bangladesh Bank.
On
body_html:
The exchange rate of the US dollar in Bangladesh’s banking channels has crossed Tk 125, driven by a surge in demand for fuel and petroleum imports, defying various stabilization measures by Bangladesh Bank.

On Tuesday (Nov 10), several commercial banks purchased US dollars from exchange houses at rates ranging between Tk 125.10 and Tk 125.15. Meanwhile, the dollar rate for settling import letters of credit (LCs) stood between Tk 124.90 and Tk 124.97. Over the past three months, the price of the dollar has escalated by more than Tk 2.30.

An official of foreign exchange department of Bangladesh Bank told UNB that the central bank has a target to keep exchange rates below Tk125.

The official not responsible for talking with the media also said that dollar exchange rates soared due to increased import demand of essentials and fuel oil.

According to bankers, the heightened demand is primarily fueled by government-level payments for fuel oil imports. Following the outbreak of conflict in the Middle East in March, international fuel prices have risen steeply, pushing current import costs to around $148 per barrel, compared to below $90 prior to the war.

Central bank data reveals that Bangladesh's total import expenditure increased by 15 percent during the July–September quarter of the current fiscal year. Petroleum import costs reached $2.98 billion during the period, up from $2.33 billion in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal year. Furthermore, expenditure on petroleum, oil, and lubricants (POL) surged to $3.71 billion—nearly double the $1.82 billion recorded a year earlier.

Despite selling $122 million from foreign exchange reserves last week, the central bank was unable to drive down the dollar rate in the open market. Financial analysts and bankers note that sustained import payment pressures from the Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation (BPC) and Petrobangla are expected to keep dollar demand elevated throughout the month.
